prerequisites: From Electricity and Magnetism: Ability to apply the general laws of electricity. Handling of circuits with passive components at the level of voltages, currents, impedances, and admittances. Concepts of electrical power.
From Electrical Systems (developed in the same semester, but this content is chronologically synchronized): Fundamental laws and theorems of electrical circuits.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to identify the applications and functions of Electronics in Engineering.
Ability to recognize the basic electronic components and devices used in electronic applications.
Ability to analyze analog, power, and digital electronic circuits.
Ability to use basic analysis techniques for analog, digital, and power electronic circuits.
Ability to handle the instruments of a basic electronics laboratory.
Ability to use electronic circuit simulation tools.

syllabus_topics: Basic laboratory instrumentation and simulation tools
Operational Amplifier: Introduction. Models. Analysis of circuits with O.A.
Applications of O.A. in open loop.
Linear applications of O.A. Basic stages.
Applications of O.A. with positive feedback.
Introduction to the transistor. Operation as amplifier and as switch.
Digital Electronics and Introduction to the Microprocessor.
Problems and exercises for Digital Electronics.
Introduction to devices used in P.E. Operation as switches.
Basic analysis techniques for power electronic circuits in non-sinusoidal periodic regime.
Fourier Series and their application in Power Electronics.
Power in non-sinusoidal periodic current and voltage regime.
AC-DC Converters. Rectification and filtering. Applications.
Four-quadrant DC-AC Converters. Switching strategies. Applications.
Four-quadrant DC-DC Converters. Switching strategies. Applications.
Problems and exercises for Power Electronics.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a score higher than 35% of the maximum grade must be obtained in the written test for each of the course's thematic blocks. The final grade is calculated according to the specified assessment criteria. If the criterion of scoring higher than 35% of the maximum grade in each of the written test blocks is not met, the maximum final grade will be 4.5 out of 10. For part-time students, non-recoverable assessment activities may be replaced by others, to be specified in each case, provided the reason is related to their part-time recognition.
